frontmatter_raw:
name: <slug>
description: <What it does and when to use it, in one or two sentences. This is what an agent matches on. At most 1,024 characters.>
version: 1.0.0

name: learn-my-brand
description: >-
  Learn my brand once and stop asking me every time. Use when someone says learn my brand, set up my brand,
  here's our brand book, remember how we talk, what can we claim, can we say this, approve our claims,
  sign off our voice, our price or product changed, the client approved the claims, pick up where we left off,
  or check our claims are still current. Reads what GooseWorks already found about the brand, asks only the
  gaps as drafts to confirm, audits every claim (including ones research marked approved) and gets the ones
  that matter signed off with proof, scope and review date, turns the voice into rules the owner confirms,
  checks logo, colours and fonts, and saves it all as it goes so every other job loads it instead of asking.
  Ends with an unknowns list and a read-back. Not for who our customers are and what they say (use
  research-audience) or writing positioning from scratch (not covered yet).

name: make-product-photos
description: >-
  Use when the marketer says: studio photos of my product without a shoot, product photos for my store page, packshots on white, lifestyle or on-model shots, photos for the new colourway, fresh product imagery for ads, photos for our launch page, our packaging changed — redo the photos, I have no photographer. Delivers store-ready product photos generated from the brand's real product photos: a shot list built from the page slots (hero, alt angle, scale, detail, in use, lifestyle, on-model), only real photos of this product as references, matched to the brand's photography, every shot checked against the real product for shape, parts, logo, text, colour, finish, scale and honest representation, with a keep / maybe / reject verdict and a page order. The human picks the keepers. Never uploads to a store, never shows a size, part, feature or result the product lacks. Not for ads with text, infographics or screenshots — make-static-ads; not for marketplace listing sets (not covered yet).

name: make-video-ads
description: >-
  Use when the marketer says: make me a video ad, a 30-second ad for paid social, a Reel / TikTok / Shorts ad, a UGC-style video made with AI (no real creator), a product demo video, remake this ad I like for my brand, cut our best organic video into an ad, more like my winning video with new hooks, my video ad got rejected — fix it. Delivers a produced, ready-to-post video ad grounded in a researched angle: one message, a hook for the first two seconds, every claim traced to the brand's signed-off claims, no generated person posing as a customer, the exact words and the price approved before anything renders (one video, or one plus two hook variants), an honest review of the result, priced fixes only on a yes, and launch copy and notes for the ads team. Works in chat apps. Never publishes or spends ad budget. Not for real creators filming for you — work-with-creators (unsure? ask: AI-made or a real person); not for a phone-shot organic post — run-organic-social; not for static ads — make-static-ads.

name: goose-ads
slug: goose-ads
description: Edit, resize, animate and study image ads with GooseWorks in this chat. New static or image ads go to the make-static-ads skill when it is installed or catalog_fetch opens it. Read the brand and follow the active playbook, preserving factual prerequisites and approvals.
version: 3.2.2
author: GooseWorks

name: goose-product-photos
slug: goose-product-photos
description: Make product photos (studio, lifestyle or on a model) of a brand's real products with GooseWorks in this chat. Start brand work with brand_knowledge_browse and follow the next_step in every answer.
version: 1.1.0
author: GooseWorks

name: goose-video-local
description: Make an approved GooseWorks video when an answer's next_step gives its command.
version: 1.0.3

name: goose-video
description: "Make a video ad in this chat from a real reference ad, found or theirs; styles are the fallback. Follow every answer's next_step."
version: 4.5.2

name: gooseworks
slug: gooseworks
description: >
  GooseWorks growth coworker and router for markets, competitors, audiences, creators,
  campaigns, ads, photos, graphics, video, content, email, SEO, social, leads and contacts.
  Use for brand facts or copy too, so offers, prices, rules, audience and bestsellers
  reach the brand's Marketing Brain.
version: 2.2.3
author: GooseWorks
tags: [gooseworks, data, scraping, search, research, gtm, leads, prospecting, ads, video]

name: make-custom-video
description: "Create a custom video with sourced product accuracy, explicit sound routing and exact-final audiovisual review."
version: 3.8.3
requires_skills: [video-production-harness, ad-angle-miner, comment-mining, competitor-ad-intelligence, create-video-fal, create-video-seedance-2-fal, media-proxy, reddit-post-finder, render-street-interview, scrapecreators-api, transcript-intelligence, watch, write-video-ad-script]
harness_binding: gooseworks/video-actions/v1

name: ad-policy-check
description: >-
  Checks paid ads against the ad platform's rules (Meta, TikTok, Google, LinkedIn and others) and the
  brand's category rules: the copy, on-image or on-screen text, pictures and people. Rewrites what can
  be fixed honestly, adds the disclosures that are needed, and flags anything that needs a human or
  legal review, with one pass, fixed or flag line per ad and platform. Use alone when you already have
  the ad text or images and know where they will run; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g.
  make-static-ads, make-content, email-lifecycle).
version: 0.1.3

name: analyze-performance-call-and-learn
description: >-
  Step of the analyze-performance playbook: calls ended tests, scores last week's calls, writes this
  week's kill/scale/hold calls and drafts learnings for the brand brain. Run analyze-performance
  instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: analyze-performance-diagnose
description: >-
  Step of the analyze-performance playbook: flags tracking breaks with fixes and explains each big
  metric move with evidence, confidence and ruled-out causes. Run analyze-performance instead; not for
  direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: analyze-performance-intake
description: >-
  Step of the analyze-performance playbook: gathers the week's numbers from tools, exports and pastes,
  cleans them, and writes the coverage line or switches to claims-only mode. Run analyze-performance
  instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: analyze-performance-rank-and-read
description: >-
  Step of the analyze-performance playbook: ranks creative by angle, hook and format with spend gates,
  writes short per-channel reads and drafts what to make next. Run analyze-performance instead; not
  for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: analyze-performance-revenue-join
description: >-
  Step of the analyze-performance playbook: joins cleaned store or CRM numbers with ad spend to build
  the business-truth table, MER, new-customer cost and the overclaim ratio. Run analyze-performance
  instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: analyze-performance
description: >-
  Weekly performance read across every channel we run: what worked, why, and what to make next, judged
  on the business's real number (store revenue, qualified pipeline, retained users), not platform
  claims. Use when: write my Monday report; how are my ads doing — which ad won?; are my ads actually
  making money (Meta says 4x ROAS but revenue is flat); why did sales drop this week; did the test
  win; is my tracking working; monthly numbers for the replan; anything on fire today. Not for acting
  on the recommendations (pausing, scaling, launching) — use run-paid-campaigns; not for replanning
  the budget — use plan-campaign.
version: 0.1.2

name: claims-gate
description: >-
  Checks every claim in a piece of copy (ads, emails, posts, pages, scripts, briefs) against the
  claims the brand has approved. Keeps, rewrites or cuts each line, and lists the proof that would
  bring a cut line back. When a line the copy needs has no approval, it asks for a short sign-off on
  the 3 or 4 lines that matter and records the answer. Use alone when you already have the copy and a
  brand set up; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. make-static-ads, make-content,
  write-outreach).
version: 0.1.6

name: email-lifecycle-broadcast-planner
description: >-
  Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: builds the month's send calendar and writes this week's email
  and SMS broadcasts against the approved cadence and segments. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for
  direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: email-lifecycle-flow-writer
description: >-
  Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: writes one lifecycle flow as a build sheet for the brand's
  email tool, every message finished in the brand voice. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct
  use.
version: 0.1.1

name: email-lifecycle-lifecycle-audit
description: >-
  Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: audits list, consent, live flows, recent sends and sending
  setup, marking every item verified, from-you or unknown. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct
  use.
version: 0.1.1

name: email-lifecycle-offer-math
description: >-
  Prices one discount, free-shipping threshold or referral reward against contribution margin: cost
  per order, share of margin used, break-even lift, code leakage risks, and one recommended offer in
  two plain sentences. Use alone when you already have the offer, average order value and margin per
  product; otherwise run email-lifecycle.
version: 0.1.1

name: email-lifecycle-send-check
description: >-
  Checks a drafted email flow or broadcast before it is loaded: flow logic and exits, overlaps, offer
  depth and codes, stock, claims, consent and legal footer, SMS rules, rendering, voice and AI-copy
  tells, and the goal metric. Returns a pass / fixed / open-question table. Use alone when you already
  have the finished draft and the brand's product and policy facts; otherwise run email-lifecycle.
version: 0.1.1

name: email-lifecycle
description: >-
  Lifecycle email, SMS and push: audits the list and deliverability, then writes the flows this kind
  of business needs first, loadable as-is in your own tool, plus segments, cadence and this week's
  broadcasts. Never sends anything. Use when: set up my welcome and abandoned-cart emails; trial
  onboarding or waitlist launch emails; win back lapsed customers; plan this week's emails and texts;
  push notifications for my app; why are my emails going to spam; plan our Black Friday email and SMS
  sends; a send went wrong. Not for cold outreach to prospects — use write-outreach; not the editorial
  newsletter issue — use make-content; not the whole cross-channel Black Friday plan — use
  plan-campaign.
version: 0.1.1

name: honest-review
description: >-
  Shared step of the marketing playbooks (make-static-ads, run-organic-social): how to review
  generated images and video honestly. Covers what was seen by eye versus read automatically, findings
  framed as things for the human to confirm, remakes only after a yes to the price, and at most two
  tries per item. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.3

name: improve-search-visibility-citation-check
description: >-
  Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: runs the agreed buyer questions on AI and Google
  surfaces, records every run and scores how often the brand is named. Run improve-search-visibility
  instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: improve-search-visibility-entity-footprint
description: >-
  Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: checks the profiles answer engines read, plus local
  listings and reviews, against the brand's facts and writes corrections. Run
  improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: improve-search-visibility-fix-writer
description: >-
  Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: turns one ranked fix into paste-ready site copy or
  code with owner, risk and undo, and writes page briefs. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not
  for direct use.
version: 0.2.1

name: improve-search-visibility-page-and-foundation-check
description: >-
  Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: audits site indexing, crawling, technical and page
  issues at the requested scope, or checks pages behind lost visibility questions. Run improve-search-visibility instead;
  not for direct use.
version: 0.2.1

name: improve-search-visibility-question-set
description: >-
  Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: drafts and scores the buyer-question set in AI and
  Google forms and groups it into page clusters. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct
  use.
version: 0.1.1

name: improve-search-visibility-store-listing-audit
description: >-
  Audits an app's App Store and Google Play listing against three competitors (title, subtitle,
  description opening, first screenshots and captions, rating, review themes) and writes a
  field-by-field rewrite with character counts, or a launch-day listing before release. Use alone when
  you already have the app's store links and signed-off product facts; otherwise run
  improve-search-visibility.
version: 0.1.1

name: improve-search-visibility
description: >-
  SEO and AI-answer visibility. Use for a site SEO or technical audit with ranked fixes,
  competitor keyword and topic gaps, a topic cluster, SEO metrics for domains, a programmatic
  SEO page-set plan, or checking where ChatGPT and Google name the brand. Delivers the requested
  audit, comparison, map or blueprint with dated evidence and clear data limits. Also covers app
  store listings and local search. Drafts changes; never edits live. Full pages go to make-content;
  paid search goes to run-paid-campaigns.
version: 0.2.1

name: make-content-content-brief
description: >-
  Writes a one-page content brief before any draft: audience, intent, the one arguable point, what top
  results already say and what this piece adds, an outline, a proof inventory with gaps marked, voice,
  CTA and banned words, checked against six gates. Use alone when you already have the topic, format,
  audience and destination and want only the brief; otherwise run make-content.
version: 0.1.1

name: make-content-source-to-units
description: >-
  Step of the make-content playbook: mines one finished asset into scored quotable units and maps a
  different lead unit to each platform. Run make-content instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: make-content-two-pass-edit
description: >-
  Edits an existing draft in order: a substance pass (arguable thesis, swap test, fakes removed, CTA
  fit), a claims and fact check that cuts or softens unproven lines, a readability and voice-match
  pass, then an AI-tell sweep, with an edit note listing open gaps. Use alone when you already have a
  finished draft and the brand's voice samples and approved claims; otherwise run make-content.
version: 0.1.2

name: make-content
description: >-
  Writes marketing content: articles, single posts, newsletters, scripts and repurposed cuts, each
  with an edit note and a claims check. Use when a marketer says "write a blog post / case study",
  "write a LinkedIn or X post / thread / X article", "carousel copy", "draft this week's newsletter",
  "turn this webinar into posts" or "repurpose this", "write a TikTok or YouTube script", "refresh
  this old post", or "write the page from this SEO brief". Words only; nothing is invented or
  published. Not for a dated posting calendar — use run-organic-social; not ad copy (make-static-ads)
  or promo emails (email-lifecycle). Press releases, landing and product pages, and sales decks are
  not covered.
version: 0.1.2

name: make-static-ads-ad-copy
description: >-
  Step of make-static-ads: writes the text for each slot the ad's template sets, then the primary texts, headline, description and CTA around the image, from usable facts and customer words. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.9.1

name: make-static-ads-claims-extract
description: >-
  Step of the make-static-ads playbook: pulls every claim-bearing span out of an ad — the copy around the image, the on-image words in the prompt, badges, and what the picture implies — and keeps or cuts each by the brand-brain rule. Runs before spend on the finished prompt (Pass A) and on every render (Pass B). Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.9.1

name: make-static-ads-compose
description: >-
  Step of make-static-ads: writes each ad's render prompt and ordered image list from its concept-board row, one per ad and ratio, ready for a quoted render. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.10.2

name: make-static-ads-concept-grid
description: >-
  Step of make-static-ads: turns the chosen angles into messages, visual ideas and a template per ad, checks each against the brand profile and recent ads, writes the concept board and has a fresh critic attack it before any copy, prompt or spend. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.10.1

name: make-static-ads-copy-variants
description: >-
  Step of the make-static-ads playbook: after an image is approved, makes more versions of the same picture with different hooks, headlines or fonts by a quoted re-render with the approved render attached as the brand's own image, so copy can be tested without new visuals. Offered, never default. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.9.1

name: make-static-ads-find-references
description: >-
  Step of make-static-ads: picks a template for every ad in its chosen style, after its visual idea and style are set, from the brand's own ads, the GooseWorks library or category leaders, and records what the chosen creativity level keeps from it. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.10.2

name: make-static-ads-fix-rejected
description: >-
  Step of the make-static-ads playbook: fixes a static image ad the platform rejected — finds the ad, maps the platform's reason to the line or element at fault, fixes copy for free or re-composes the image text on a quote, re-runs the claims and policy checks, and answers the request. A rejected video is the video playbook's job. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.9.1

name: make-static-ads-graphic-request
description: >-
  Makes one simple non-ad brand graphic, such as an email header, social feed or story image, or a
  blog or link-preview image, in the brand's style with at most a short line of text, after claim and
  rights checks and a yes to the quote; returns the link and alt text. Not for carousels, decks or
  print. Use alone when you already have the purpose, placement and exact wording; otherwise run
  make-static-ads.
version: 0.9.1

name: make-static-ads-render-review
description: >-
  Step of make-static-ads: a fresh judge checks every render against its concept-board row and the official product photos, one retry inside the marketer's approval, then the claims and set checks; records each verdict in tags and the batch file. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.10.1

name: make-static-ads
description: >-
  Make new static image ads, a fresh batch, more ads, a winner's variations, copy variants or a rejected ad fix. Reads the brand, its customers and the ads it already runs, turns real product facts and customer situations into distinct visual ideas, shows a concept board, writes each render prompt, quotes, renders and reviews through GooseWorks. Also handles requested branded header/social graphics. Use for static ad creation rather than goose-ads. Not for video, product photos or launching campaigns.
version: 0.10.3

name: marketing-data-access
description: >-
  How to get live public data (ads libraries, social posts and comments, search results, creator
  profiles), business identity/work-contact reads, domain SEO metrics and paid media generation through GooseWorks, with no vendor key. Load before any playbook
  step that reads public data or calls an outside model: which proxy call fits the job, what it costs,
  how to get the human's yes, and what to do when the data is not reachable. Not for brand facts (read
  the brand brain) or the customer's own ad accounts (the GooseWorks ads tools, or an ads connector
  they have).
version: 0.1.2

name: marketing-guide
description: >-
  How every GooseWorks marketing playbook runs: connecting, picking the brand, where files go, the
  shared claims, money, research and schedule rules, and the index of what each playbook saves and who
  reads it. Load at the start of any playbook run. Not a marketer ask: for "what should I do first?"
  use where-to-start.
version: 0.1.4

name: outcomes-ledger
description: >-
  Shared step of the marketing playbooks (research-audience, write-outreach, work-with-creators):
  keeps the brand's record of the prospects or creators that were handed over. Tracks a status for
  each person, permanent opt-outs, re-check dates and dated lessons, which the next run reads. Loaded
  by those playbooks; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: plan-campaign-brief-and-assets
description: >-
  Step of the plan-campaign playbook: writes angles per channel, the asset list, measurement plan,
  hand-offs and replan triggers, then assembles the plan. Run plan-campaign instead; not for direct
  use.
version: 0.1.2

name: plan-campaign-budget-and-tests
description: >-
  Step of the plan-campaign playbook: splits the budget across chosen channels, checks per-channel
  minimums, and writes the test plan and paid structure. Run plan-campaign instead; not for direct
  use.
version: 0.1.2

name: plan-campaign-channel-decision
description: >-
  Step of the plan-campaign playbook: marks each candidate channel Run, Test, Later or No with a
  brand-fact reason and founder hours. Run plan-campaign instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: plan-campaign-goal-chain
description: >-
  Checks whether a stated goal is reachable on a given budget: fills an economics box with a source on
  every number, subtracts the baseline, works out the implied cost per customer against history or
  labelled base rates, and flags when the goal needs renegotiating. Use alone when you already have
  the goal (metric, number, date), budget, order value, margin and baseline; otherwise run
  plan-campaign.
version: 0.1.2

name: plan-campaign
description: >-
  Campaign planner: turns a product, offer, goal, budget and date into a plan the marketer can approve
  and a designer can start from today, with every channel kept or dropped for a reason. Zero paid is a
  valid answer; it never spends. Use when the ask names a campaign, a launch, drop or season push, a
  budget or a date: I have this budget and a launch date — what do I run, where?; plan my launch, drop
  or Black Friday push; plan a campaign; how should I split $5k; plan next month's campaign; our CAC
  blew up — replan. Not for a broad "grow my brand", "get more customers" or "where do I start" with
  no campaign, budget or date — use where-to-start; not for pausing ads on a sold-out product — use
  run-paid-campaigns; not for an email-only send plan — use email-lifecycle; not for reading this
  week's numbers — use analyze-performance.
version: 0.1.4

name: research-audience-account-sourcing
description: >-
  Step of the research-audience playbook: finds candidate accounts matching the fit definition,
  confirms gates, applies exclusions and dedupes. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-audience-fit-definition
description: >-
  Step of the research-audience playbook: drafts the searchable fit definition, exclusions and list
  size that the list run then searches on. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-audience-people-and-contacts
description: >-
  For a list of companies, picks 1-3 current people per company in different buying roles, confirms
  each title with a dated source, finds a public contact route, labels email status honestly and flags
  regions with contact rules. Never contacts anyone. Use alone when you already have a vetted company
  list and the buyer titles; otherwise run research-audience.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-audience-score-segment-qa
description: >-
  Step of the research-audience playbook: scores and tiers list rows, groups them into segments with
  an angle each, runs the pre-handover checks and writes the list files. Run research-audience
  instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-audience-segment-pass
description: >-
  Step of the research-audience playbook: the worker brief for researching one buyer group, returning
  notes in a fixed shape. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-audience-signals-and-hooks
description: >-
  For a list of companies, finds dated, linked timing signals from the last 90 days (funding, new
  leaders, hiring, launches), drops stale ones and noise, scores timing, and gives one personal hook
  per person from their recent public work. Facts only, no message copy. Use alone when you already
  have the company list and, for hooks, the people; otherwise run research-audience.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-audience
description: >-
  Audience research: who the buyers are, in their own words, where they gather and how to reach them —
  plus named prospect lists when asked. Use when the marketer says "research our audience", "who
  should we target", "mine our reviews", "why do people buy us or leave", "where does our audience
  hang out"; or for lists: "find 50 right-fit leads with emails", "find retailers or accounts to
  pitch", "score these leads / who do we call first", "who's looking for an alternative to X", "tell
  me when a past champion changes jobs". Reads the brand's own customer data first and delivers a
  readable report saved to the brand. Never contacts anyone. Not for market size or trends — use
  research-market; not for writing the messages — use write-outreach.
version: 0.8.3

name: research-competitors-category-pass
description: >-
  Step of the research-competitors playbook: the worker brief covering the whole category, including
  searches, AI answers, community threads and category ad winners. Run research-competitors instead;
  not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-competitors-edge-cases
description: >-
  Step of the research-competitors playbook: rules for run edge cases such as no browser, stalled
  workers, earlier reports and late reads. Run research-competitors instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-competitors-rival-pass
description: >-
  Step of the research-competitors playbook: the worker brief for profiling one rival at a capped
  depth, returning a fixed-shape profile. Run research-competitors instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-competitors
description: >-
  Competitor research: what every main rival is running, launching, charging and saying now, what
  works for them, and what that means for you. Use when the marketer asks for competitor research or a
  teardown, "what ads are my competitors running", "how do they price", "find gaps and angles", "what
  changed this week" (a weekly watch), or "X just launched / shut down / cut prices" (react now). Also builds a sales battlecard, checks a
  competitor page's tools/pixels, or studies who engages with their LinkedIn posts.
  Delivers a readable report saved to the brand, so the next run reports what changed. Never copies
  their words or disparages them. Not for what people say about you or your market — use
  research-market; not for who your buyers are — use research-audience.
version: 0.5.1

name: research-market-edge-cases
description: >-
  Step of the research-market playbook: rules for run edge cases such as no browser, stalled workers,
  earlier reports and late reads. Run research-market instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-market-listening
description: >-
  Step of the research-market playbook: the worker brief for listening to what people say about the
  brand and category, risks first. Run research-market instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: research-market-market-pass
description: >-
  Step of the research-market playbook: the worker brief for researching the market itself, including
  category, size, changes, pricing norms and demand. Run research-market instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: research-market
description: >-
  Market research and brand watch: which market the brand is in, how big the reachable part is, what's
  changing, how buyers buy and what they pay, what people are saying now, and what it means for
  positioning. Use when the marketer asks for market research, "how big is my market", "what's
  changing in my category", "what do others charge", "what are people saying about us", "is there
  demand for <idea>", or "watch my brand / tell me if something blows up" (alerts only, risk first).
  Also writes positioning choices and finished messages ("position my product", "write our positioning").
  Researches first, asks only decisions at the end, and saves the output to the brand.
  Not for who the buyers are and their own words — use research-audience; not for a deep look at
  rivals — use research-competitors.
version: 0.5.1

name: run-memory
description: >-
  Shared step of the marketing playbooks (analyze-performance, run-paid-campaigns,
  research-competitors, email-lifecycle): reads the last run's record, checks whether its
  recommendations were done and whether they worked, and saves a short record of this run for the next
  one. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.3

name: run-organic-social-account-audit
description: >-
  Reviews a brand's own social accounts: what each is for, the last ~30 posts ranked against the
  account's own median with the likely reason for top and bottom posts, cadence actually kept, best
  posting times, and bio and pinned-post fixes. Use alone when you already know which accounts to
  review and can read their posts; otherwise run run-organic-social.
version: 0.1.1

name: run-organic-social-plan-calendar
description: >-
  Step of the run-organic-social playbook: turns the audit, research and dated moments into a two-week
  grid of empty post slots. Run run-organic-social instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: run-organic-social-platform-research
description: >-
  Researches how one social platform works right now from dated sources (what gets reach, formats
  rising and fading, how small accounts get seen, recent changes) and finds what is getting watched in
  a given niche there, with linked examples and engagement read against each author's baseline. Use
  alone when you already have the platform and niche; otherwise run run-organic-social.
version: 0.1.1

name: run-organic-social-post-check
description: >-
  Checks a draft social post before it goes out: voice match against the account, would a person
  actually post it, AI-sounding phrases, claims against what the brand has signed off, banned words,
  disclosure and rights, trend timing, and whether a named person must approve it; rewrites weak
  drafts. Use alone when you already have the draft, the brand's voice and approved claims; otherwise
  run run-organic-social.
version: 0.1.1

name: run-organic-social
description: >-
  Runs a brand's organic social: how each platform works now, a strategy per platform and two weeks of
  posts in the brand's or a person's real voice. Use when a marketer says "run organic social for my
  brand", "fill my social calendar", "plan two weeks of posts", "grow my X / LinkedIn / Instagram /
  TikTok", "ghostwrite my founder's posts", "which platforms should we be on?", "plan the social for
  our launch", "a TikTok or Reel script to shoot on my phone", "tear down @x's account", or "my
  accounts went quiet". The marketer posts by hand; nothing is posted or scheduled. Not for a
  standalone post or repurposing one piece — use make-content.
version: 0.1.2

name: run-paid-campaigns-apply-and-log
description: >-
  Step of the run-paid-campaigns playbook: stages the week's approval items, applies only what the
  marketer approves and keeps the change log. Run run-paid-campaigns instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: run-paid-campaigns-draft-moves
description: >-
  Step of the run-paid-campaigns playbook: turns the weekly read into scale, pause, hold, rotate and
  fix recommendations within the spend ceiling. Run run-paid-campaigns instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: run-paid-campaigns-health-gate
description: >-
  Checks that ads are safe to spend on: conversion tracking recording, landing pages loading on mobile
  with the right product, price and offer, enough stock behind promoted products, no disapproved ads,
  and no account or payment stop. Marks each pass, fail or unknown and turns fails into fixes. Use
  alone when you already have the live or planned ads and their landing pages; otherwise run
  run-paid-campaigns.
version: 0.1.2

name: run-paid-campaigns-weekly-read
description: >-
  Step of the run-paid-campaigns playbook: reads each platform's last mature results window against
  the allowable cost, as evidence for the week's moves. Run run-paid-campaigns instead; not for direct
  use.
version: 0.1.2

name: run-paid-campaigns
description: >-
  Runs the paid leg of an approved plan: checks tracking, pages and stock before money moves, then
  stages one weekly proposal of kills, scales, pauses, swaps and launches, each with its reason and a
  check date. Nothing changes without your yes. Use when: launch these ads; it's Monday — kill, scale
  or pause?; swap this fatiguing ad; we sold out or the sale ended — pause the ads now; an ad got
  rejected or the account got restricted; we're in a brand crisis — hold the ads; give me the Google,
  TikTok or LinkedIn changes to make. Not for how the ads did or which ad won — use
  analyze-performance; not for rewriting a rejected image ad — use make-static-ads.
version: 0.1.2

name: save-learning
description: >-
  Shared step of the marketing playbooks (make-static-ads, analyze-performance, email-lifecycle,
  write-outreach): saves a short brand rule or finding in the human's own words, one idea per rule,
  retires the playbook's own older rules it replaces, and reads the result back to confirm. Loaded by
  those playbooks; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.3

name: save-to-brain
description: >-
  Shared step of the marketing playbooks (research-market, plan-campaign, make-content,
  analyze-performance): saves a finished file to the brand and makes it searchable. It either replaces
  older versions or keeps dated history, then checks that the file can be found. Loaded by those
  playbooks; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: spend-gate
description: >-
  Shared step of the marketing playbooks (make-static-ads, research-market, run-paid-campaigns,
  work-with-creators): gets the human's yes before any credits are spent. Shows the price exactly as
  quoted, or asks for one yes to a credit ceiling for paid data reads, stays under it and logs each
  charge. Also covers scheduled runs. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.2

name: voice-card
description: >-
  Builds or updates a voice card from a company blog ("extract our blog voice") or how an account or
  person actually writes, measured from about 8 or
  more of their real posts (length, casing, emoji, openings, pet phrases, opinions with their source).
  When there are too few posts, it runs a short interview instead. It ends with a test that checks a
  draft against the card. The brand's rules always beat the card. Use alone when you already have the
  account's posts or the person on hand; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g.
  run-organic-social, write-outreach, email-lifecycle).
version: 0.2.1

name: where-to-start-situation-save
description: >-
  Step of the where-to-start playbook: saves the founder's answers and the agreed first move with the
  brand, so later visits and other playbooks don't ask again. Run where-to-start instead; not for
  direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: where-to-start
description: >-
  First-move advice for a broad growth or marketing ask with no job named: looks at what GooseWorks
  already knows and at the site, asks a few short questions in one message, names the one thing in
  the way, and sends the marketer to the right next job. Use when the marketer says "help me grow my
  brand", "I need to grow my business", "how do I get more customers / sales", "help me with
  marketing", "where do I start", "sales are flat", "what should I focus on this month", or "I'm back,
  what's next?". Recommends only; never runs the work. Not for a named job like "make me ads" or "grow
  my Instagram" (go straight to it); not for a campaign with a launch, budget or date — use
  plan-campaign; not for why this week's numbers moved — use analyze-performance.
version: 0.1.4

name: work-with-creators-brief-writer
description: >-
  Writes a one-page brief for one creator you have already picked: hook ideas in their format, at most
  three approved must-say lines, never-says, the disclosure for their platform, deliverables,
  timeline, the usage-rights ask and two examples. Adds a short first-message draft (gift and paid
  versions) for you to send. Use alone when you already have the creator, their best fitting post and
  the goal; otherwise run work-with-creators.
version: 0.1.1

name: work-with-creators-creator-discovery
description: >-
  Step of the work-with-creators playbook: builds and screens a long list of creators from fans,
  category creators and search, and ranks finalists to vet next. Run work-with-creators instead; not
  for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: work-with-creators-creator-vetting
description: >-
  Vets creators you have already named from their public pages. Covers the median views of their last
  12 to 20 posts (sponsored and organic apart), a read of their comments, how often they post,
  audience fit with how sure it is, about 12 months of brand-safety checks, rival partnerships and
  rules for regulated categories. Gives a verdict with dated numbers for each one. Use alone when you
  already have the creator handles and the brand's goal; otherwise run work-with-creators.
version: 0.1.1

name: work-with-creators-rate-and-deal
description: >-
  Prices a creator you have already vetted. Gives a low and a target fee from median views and the
  platform's typical cost per 1,000 views, a walk-away ceiling from your goal and margin, and usage
  rights priced on their own. Checks against real quoted rates and recommends gift, paid, affiliate or
  a mix, with one line showing the math. Use alone when you already have the creator's recent view
  numbers, your goal and your unit cost; otherwise run work-with-creators.
version: 0.1.1

name: work-with-creators
description: >-
  Real creators and influencers, researched, priced and briefed. Use when the marketer says "find
  influencers", "which creators are worth paying, at what price?", "find real UGC creators to film for
  our ads", "who should we seed product to", "is this creator's engagement real", "what should I pay
  this creator" or "write a creator brief". Free research first; one credit yes only to vet deeper.
  Drafts only: contacts nobody, agrees nothing, moves no money. Not for AI-made UGC-style video —
  use goose-video; if unsure, ask: a real person filming, or AI-made?
version: 0.4.2

name: write-outreach-draft-sequence
description: >-
  Step of the write-outreach playbook: the brief a helper follows to write one segment's email and
  LinkedIn sequence, first lines and replies from rows and an angle prepared earlier. Run
  write-outreach instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: write-outreach-outreach-qa
description: >-
  Step of the write-outreach playbook: the checks a finished outreach pack and send file must pass
  before delivery, covering facts, proof, compliance, length, asks and tone. Run write-outreach
  instead; not for direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: write-outreach-reply-reader
description: >-
  Step of the write-outreach playbook: sorts outreach replies by type, matches each to its prospect
  row, sets that person's status and keeps useful exact words. Run write-outreach instead; not for
  direct use.
version: 0.1.1

name: write-outreach
description: >-
  Cold outreach a person sends to business buyers: email and LinkedIn sequences, a first line per
  prospect, reply and objection answers, and a read of replies. Use when the marketer says "write a
  cold email sequence", "what do I send to this list", "write LinkedIn messages for these leads", "how
  do I reply to this prospect" or "handle this objection", "reply to this demo request", "win back or
  reconnect with accounts that churned or went quiet", or "why is nobody replying to my outreach".
  Drafts only; the marketer sends from their own tool. Not for finding the people — use
  research-audience; not for emails to subscribers or users, or consumer win-back — use
  email-lifecycle.
version: 0.2.2

name: write-report
description: >-
  Turns findings you already have into a report a marketer can read in 30 seconds. It has a short
  summary with key findings and how sure each one is, the first move, decisions needed, at most six
  next moves, what was not checked, and dated sources. It checks length and wording before handing
  over, then saves the report to the brand. Use alone when you already have the findings and their
  sources; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. research-market, research-competitors,
  plan-campaign).
version: 0.1.2

name: ad-angle-miner
description: Research supported advertising promises from a specific buyer's context, current product facts, customer language and observed ads. Turn them into static, video or copy ideas; match video ideas to actual recipes and save a product-scoped angle bank for write-video-ad-script. Product-led discovery can use verified facts without reviews. Reference persistence and reach are observations, not proof of performance.

name: ad-campaign-analyzer
description: >
  Analyze ad campaign performance data (Google, Meta, LinkedIn) to identify what's
  working, what's wasting budget, and specific cut/scale/test recommendations. Runs
  statistical analysis, funnel diagnostics, and multi-channel budget reallocation
  with specific dollar-amount shift recommendations and scenario modeling.

name: ad-lead-quality-analyzer
description: For paid lead-gen and participant-recruitment ads, replaces vanity CPA with true CAC per qualified lead by joining ad-platform data with downstream funnel events, surfaces tracking gaps, and classifies every creative into Scale / Keep / Investigate / Cut.

name: ad-management-intake
description: The intake stage of a Meta ad harness. Researches the brand first, states what it assumes, and asks only what it cannot infer and what would change money, claims or legal exposure if guessed wrong — at most four questions a turn, in plain business language. Writes the brand's stable facts (ads/brand.md), the campaign brief, and a log of what was asked vs assumed. Use it when someone wants to run Meta ads and the brand's ad facts are not yet recorded.

name: ads-north-star-strategy
description: Turn a brand's facts, a campaign brief and the product into a one-minute Meta ad strategy with its reasoning — goal, audience, objective and placements, budget split, how many ads and how different they must be (generate 3x so the user can choose), the test frame, the success metric, and safety rules for the user to accept. Decides what launch-meta-ad-campaign then executes, and re-reads the strategy after a deep check to show which assumption changed. Use it after intake and before any creative is generated or any campaign is built.

name: answer-ads-questions
description: Answer questions about a brand's Meta ads (spend, results, which ad is winning, is it paused, why did Goose do that) only from reads made in the same turn, with the data window and sync time on every number and a plain caveat when the connection is stale or partial. Use it whenever a user asks how their ads are doing or why an ad action was taken.

name: brand-research
description: Research a company or brand from its website and produce a reusable Brand Core covering products, audience, competitors, positioning, offers, messaging evidence, voice, and visual identity. Use before growth, ad, content, creator, or product work when reliable brand context is missing.

name: comment-mining
description: Mine comments and replies on social posts, videos, and ads for recurring customer language, questions, objections, desired outcomes, complaints, product requests, purchase signals, and creative opportunities. Use for voice-of-customer research grounded in linked source evidence.

name: company-contact-finder
description: >
  Find decision-makers at a specific company using Fiber, Crustdata and PDL
  people search inside the GooseWorks coworker. Given a company name and target
  titles, returns a list of contacts with name, title, LinkedIn URL, and location.

name: competitor-ad-intelligence
description: >
  Scrape competitor ads from Meta, TikTok, Google, and LinkedIn ad libraries,
  analyze creative patterns (hooks, formats, CTAs), reverse-engineer landing page funnels,
  and produce a strategic teardown with vulnerability analysis and counter-play recommendations.
  Use when you need to understand the competitive ad landscape, find new creative directions,
  or identify weaknesses in a competitor's paid strategy.

name: get-brand-assets
description: Get company logos, brand colors, fonts, and style guides

name: goose-graphics-create-format
description: >
  Creates a new graphics format spec (custom canvas dimensions + content rules)
  and publishes it to the Gooseworks library so any agent can render against it.
  Use when the existing community formats (carousel, story, infographic, slides,
  poster, chart, tweet, plus community additions) don't fit the user's canvas —
  e.g., LinkedIn banner 1584×396, story cover 1080×1920, event flyer 8.5×11in.
  Mirrors goose-graphics-create-style but for formats.

name: goose-graphics-create-style
description: >
  End-to-end skill that turns a single reference image into a published
  Gooseworks style — analyzes the image, drafts the slim style spec, renders
  a hero example plus 2-3 additional formats via Playwright, writes the
  `gooseworks-style.json` manifest, and publishes via
  `npx gooseworks styles publish` so other agents can discover it. Mirrors
  goose-graphics-create-format but for styles.

name: goose-graphics
description: Portable visual skill pack for the Agent Skills ecosystem (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Claude Cowork, Claude Design, Goose, Cursor, Codex). Discovers community-published styles + formats via the gooseworks CLI, runs an extract-style workflow on reference images, and exports rendered PNGs via Playwright.

name: hacker-news-scraper
description: >
  Search Hacker News stories and comments using the free Algolia API.
  No Apify token needed. Use when you need to find HN discussions, track mentions,
  discover Show HN launches, or monitor tech community sentiment.

name: job-posting-intent
version: 1.1.1
description: >
  Detect buying intent from job postings. When a company posts a job in your problem area,
  they've allocated budget and are actively thinking about the problem. This skill finds those
  companies, qualifies them, extracts personalization context, and outputs everything to a
  Google Sheet. Does NOT do outreach — just delivers qualified leads with reasoning.

name: launch-meta-ad-campaign
description: Take someone from a business goal to a verified, paused-then-live Meta/Facebook/Instagram campaign without making them learn Meta's hierarchy. Use automatically for requests to launch, run, create, publish, set up, or plan Meta ads; use reporting skills for analysis-only requests.

name: lead-qualification
description: >
  Lead qualification engine with conversational intake. Asks structured questions to understand
  your qualification criteria, generates a reusable qualification prompt, then batch-enriches leads
  via Apify LinkedIn scraping and scores them with parallel processing. Outputs qualified/disqualified
  verdicts with confidence scores and reasoning to CSV or whatever output format the user prefers.
  Supports calibration mode for prompt refinement.

name: linkedin-profile-post-scraper
description: >
  Scrape recent posts from LinkedIn profiles using Apify. Use when you need to
  monitor what specific people are posting on LinkedIn, track founder/exec activity,
  or gather LinkedIn content for competitive intelligence.

name: meta-ad-manager
description: Front door and loop owner of a Meta (Facebook/Instagram) ad harness. Reads the brand's ads/ docs, works out which campaign the user means and which stage it is at, hands off to the stage skill that runs it (intake, strategy, creative, launch, checks, fixes, answers), and writes every stage change back to the docs. Use it when someone wants to run ads on Meta, comes back to ads they started earlier, a stage skill hands back, or a scheduled check fires.

name: meta-ad-policy-checker
description: Pre-flight policy check for Meta ads. Takes ad copy plus advertiser context, resolves and fetches the relevant Meta transparency-center policy pages at runtime, and returns a Pass / Fix Required / Block verdict with cited findings and rewrites.

name: meta-ads-analyzer
description: Diagnose Meta Ads campaign performance and account gaps using Meta's actual system mechanics — including customer-journey coverage, Breakdown Effect, Learning Phase, Auction Overlap, Pacing, and Creative Fatigue. Use for performance diagnosis, account audits, full-funnel or TOF/MOF/BOF gap analysis, deciding what to test or create next, and producing novice-friendly recommendations without forcing every campaign or ad into a funnel stage.

name: reddit-post-finder
description: Scrape and search Reddit posts using Apify. Use when you need to find Reddit discussions, track competitor mentions, monitor product feedback, discover pain points, or analyze subreddit content. Supports keyword filtering, time-based searches, and subreddit-specific queries.

name: remix-graphic-ad-from-reference
description: Recreate a static graphic ad (Pinterest pin, IG/FB feed image, poster) from a reference image, swapping in a new brand's product and new copy while keeping the reference's layout, composition, and visual energy. ALWAYS generated with GPT Image 2 in edit-the-reference mode (fal-ai/gpt-image-1/edit-image, a billed FAL generation); the HTML/goose-graphics overlay is only an optional text-finishing step, never the generator. The static-graphics counterpart to the video remix-ad skill; this is what the app calls when a user picks a reference ad and wants it for their own product.

name: scrapecreators-api
description: Provider reference for collecting public profiles, posts, comments, transcripts, trends, and ad-library data from major social platforms through ScrapeCreators. Use as a dependency of research workflows, not as the final user-facing deliverable.

name: transcript-intelligence
description: Turn TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Reddit, or Rumble transcripts into timestamped hooks, claims, objections, proof, calls to action, sponsorship signals, and reusable content atoms. Use directly for transcript analysis or as support for creator, competitor, trend, demand, and repurposing work.

name: animate-image
description: Animate an existing product image or static ad into a short branded video using the GooseWorks Animate Images workflow, with source-image continuity and optional end-frame control.

name: caption-burn
description: Burned-in captions for a finished vertical video, three kinds. transcribe.py gets word timings from the video's own audio through the GooseWorks proxy (fal Whisper, charged to your GooseWorks credits, cents); captions.py burns one to three words at a time with Pillow + ffmpeg (no libass needed), either pinned to a split-screen seam (plate 25% above / 75% below) or at a fixed height, in a plate, outline or one-word serif style, with an optional red hook card; plates.py burns per-beat caption blocks (black, one union silhouette, placed in the emptiest band) for formats with no voice. The last caption (the CTA) holds to the final frame. Use as the last step of any video ad.
status: superseded
superseded_by: captions-layer@1.1.0

name: compose-creator-layer
description: Composite a generated creator track into a product layer, per beat — in the creator's zone on split beats (either side of a seam), full frame on creator beats, hidden on product beats — with the creator's voice as the audio (loudness -14 LUFS) and an optional ducked music bed, or a music-only or silent master for voiceless formats. Free, local ffmpeg. Pairs with footage-cutlist (the layer) and create-creator-takes-h3 (the creator). Use for split-screen (with an optional zoom and brand-colour seam bar), screen-insert and any creator-over-product format.
status: active

name: create-apple-notes-mockup
description: Render pixel-accurate Apple Notes (iPhone, light mode) screenshot mockups from a JSON note spec. Outputs HTML + PNG at the iPhone 16/15 Pro native 1180×2556. Supports paragraphs, images, checklists, dividers, autocorrect underline, smart quotes, and an optional iOS keyboard chrome overlay used by the parent video-ad molecule.
status: superseded
superseded_by: phone-chat@1.2.0

name: create-chatgpt-mockup
description: Render pixel-accurate ChatGPT mobile (iOS) screen mockups in light mode from a thread JSON. Supports user text bubbles, user image attachments, assistant markdown prose, citation chips, the OpenAI spiral logo, the Apps-SDK GPT chip in the composer, and three header styles (model-tag, plain title, "Get Plus"). Fixed 9:16 viewport. Outputs HTML + PNG.
status: superseded
superseded_by: phone-chat@1.2.0

name: create-creator-takes-h3
description: Generate an AI creator talking to camera, saying an approved script, as one continuous track — H3 Max reference-to-video through the GooseWorks fal-proxy (charged to your GooseWorks credits). Plans takes on line boundaries under H3's 15s cap, dry-runs a cost estimate, generates the first take alone so its voice can be locked and passed to every later take, joins takes with measured 0.10s dissolves, and moves each line's timing onto the words actually spoken. Use for any format with a generated creator speaking a script (split-screen, screen inserts, talking-head ads).
status: superseded
version: "2.9.1"
superseded_by: creator-h3@1.8.0

name: create-image-fal
description: Generate or edit an image via any FAL image model (nano-banana edit, gpt-image, flux, ...), routed through the GooseWorks proxy, so the call is charged to your GooseWorks credits. image_urls must be public URLs; --image puts a local file on the fal CDN first. The recipe names the model + prompt. Use for keyframes, flat-cover transforms, product hero edits. (For the OpenAI gpt-image family specifically, create-image-gpt-image-fal also exists.)
status: active

name: create-image-gpt-image-fal
description: Generate a single photoreal or designed image with OpenAI gpt-image via fal.ai. Supports gpt-image-1 (default, fixed sizes — the FAL fallback for Higgsfield's `gpt_image_2`) and gpt-image-2 (`openai/gpt-image-2`, custom output sizes up to 3840px). Routes to text-to-image or the edit variant depending on whether a reference image is provided. Use for photoreal character anchors, scene keyframes, and designed sheets (e.g. storyboards) where precise layout and legible text matter.

name: create-imessage-mockup
description: Render pixel-accurate iMessage screenshot mockups (DM or group) from a thread JSON. Supports minimal, with-keyboard, and full iPhone 15 Pro frame variants. Outputs HTML + PNG.
status: superseded
superseded_by: phone-chat@1.2.0

name: create-kinetic-typography
description: Render a deterministic text-only video ad from approved copy, font, colors, timing and CTA. Use when a brand needs an animated message without product photography or a creator.

name: create-music-elevenlabs
description: Generate an instrumental music bed via ElevenLabs Music, routed through the GooseWorks proxy, so the call is charged to your GooseWorks credits. Trims any sparse intro, loudnorm, fades the tail. Prompt + length from the template recipe. Use for the music layer of any video-ad format.
status: superseded
superseded_by: music-elevenlabs@1.0.2

name: create-video-fal
description: Image-to-video (or text-to-video) via any FAL video model (Kling, Seedance, Veo), routed through the GooseWorks proxy, so the call is charged to your GooseWorks credits. The template recipe names the model + params; image_url inputs must be public URLs (the orchestrator hosts local frames with the MCP media_upload). Returns the result video URL and downloads it. Use for the generative base clip of any video-ad format.
status: active

name: create-video-seedance-2-fal
description: Generate a single 4-15s vertical video clip with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 reference-to-video via fal.ai, for shots with no realistic face (a product hero, a product in motion, an empty set). Multi-image reference (product + setting), ambient audio, internal multi-cut handling within one render, 720p by default. Routes through the GooseWorks FAL proxy (charged to your GooseWorks credits). Seedance refuses photoreal faces, so talking heads and creators go to creator-h3 / video-h3max.
status: superseded
version: "2.0.5"
superseded_by: video-seedance-2@1.3.0

name: create-vo-elevenlabs
description: Generate a voiceover (VO) clip via ElevenLabs text-to-speech, routed through the GooseWorks proxy, so the call is charged to your GooseWorks credits. Voice id + script text come from the template recipe. Use for the spoken narration of VO-driven video-ad formats (cgi-app-sizzle, flat-vector-explainer, hypermotion). Never call ElevenLabs directly — the proxy attribution is required.
status: superseded
superseded_by: voice-elevenlabs@1.3.0

name: footage-cutlist
description: Watch a brand's own product footage (screen recording, product film), pick the moment that proves each line with the user, and render those picks as a product layer — free, local. survey.py turns footage into timestamped contact sheets + scene cuts + motion so the agent can actually look at it; the agent writes a cut list (beat → source window + framing); preview.py draws it as a review sheet the user corrects round by round; cut.py renders the approved list into a silent 1080x1920 layer with the creator's area left as a plate. Also frames footage as a filmed screen (keystone, bezel, handheld drift) with dissolves between beats, and takes still screenshots as sources. Use for any format that shows real product footage beside, between or instead of a creator (split-screen, screen inserts, walkthroughs).
status: active

name: media-proxy
description: Shared helper that routes ALL paid media generation (FAL image/video, ElevenLabs music) through the GooseWorks proxies so every call is charged to your GooseWorks credits — never a provider SDK's default host. Host-swaps the FAL queue URLs, loads the agent token from the sandbox env (GW_MEDIA_PROXY_TOKEN) or ~/.gooseworks/credentials.json, and returns the result CDN URL. Every video-ad media capability imports this; templates never call a provider directly.
status: active

Transcribes the finished render's AUDIO with Whisper and word-diffs it against the approved spoken script, then gates keeping the render as the final version (video_review) — blocking a render whose generated audio mis-voices a word (e.g. the approved "human-vetted" spoken as "human witted"), says a different number or brand name, flips a negation, drops an approved phrase, or comes back silent. Correct speech written differently ("5mg" said "five milligrams", "30%" said "thirty percent", a spoken URL, "don't" said "do not", "larkfieldstraps" said "larkfield straps", a confirmed pronunciation like "TG1" said "T G one") passes. Runnable, gating counterpart to GooseWorks' fuller transcript-integrity review. Every ugc-video-formats recipe runs this after render and BEFORE keeping the final version.

name: stitch-videos-ffmpeg
description: Stitch video segments with ffmpeg concat, xfade, overlay, audio mux, and export settings, and trim a source into named clips at exact windows (trim_clips.py). Ships montage.py, a free montage assembler (python3 + ffmpeg, no keys). It takes a JSON EDL of clips and stills, normalizes them and hard-cuts them in order, burns captions from an SRT, a cue list or word timings, and lays a VO over a music bed that ducks under it, mastered to -14 LUFS.
